findings.evidence: “Pass `"$branch"` quoted. Single quotes are needed only for a literal name you type containing `$`” explains familiar shell mechanics; together with the routine branch, status and fetch instructions, this makes a substantial portion of the short workflow activation rather than expert knowledge.
findings.fix: Preserve every safety gate, but consolidate routine branch/target/clean-tree prerequisites and shorten the quoting explanation to “Always use the captured, quoted "$branch".” Retain the detailed guidance on rewritten bases, paused rebases and explicit leases.

findings.evidence: “If `$remote` is set and `git log --format=%ae "origin/$target..$remote"` lists an email other than `git config user.email`, others push to this branch: stop and ask before any mutation.” Commit authorship does not identify who pushes: collaborators can push commits authored by the current user, allowing this guard to pass before shared history is rewritten.
findings.fix: Do not infer pushership from author emails. Before rewriting an already-published branch, require confirmation that it is exclusively owned and safe to rebase; stop if it is shared. Foreign author emails may justify an additional warning, but an explicit lease protects against concurrent updates, not against rewriting known shared history.

findings.evidence: After a lease rejection, the command recommends “to inspect first, `git log "$orig..origin/$branch"`”. A rejected push does not refresh `origin/$branch`; without another fetch, it still points to the saved remote tip, which step 2 established as an ancestor of `$orig`. This inspection therefore returns no commits instead of showing the competing update.
findings.fix: Include a refresh in the suggested inspection procedure, for example `git fetch origin "refs/heads/$branch"` followed by `git log --oneline "$orig..FETCH_HEAD"`. Keep the originally captured lease value unchanged and never retry the push automatically.
